claims.text: The starting Au-Co-Cu-Ni-Pt nanoparticles are equiatomic.
The starting nanoparticles are a single-phase solid solution.
The sluggish-diffusion regime breaks down below an approximately 5 nm particle-size threshold.
The sluggish-diffusion regime breaks down above approximately 600 K.
Surface-energy minimization drives rapid segregation in the heated nanoparticles.
Ostwald ripening causes the loss of the smallest particles.
Surface-related driving forces and pathways scale inversely with particle radius and overwhelm bulk configurational-entropy stabilization.
The surface diffusion coefficient is significantly larger than the bulk diffusion coefficient because surface diffusion has a lower activation barrier.
High configurational entropy can reduce the driving force for precipitation in a single-phase high-entropy alloy.
Sluggish atomic diffusion can kinetically restrain solute segregation and precipitate growth in a single-phase high-entropy alloy.
High configurational entropy and sluggish diffusion would preserve single-phase Au-Co-Cu-Ni-Pt nanoparticles even at elevated temperature.
Low-surface-energy elements, likely Au or Pt, segregate rapidly to nanoparticle surfaces.
During Ostwald ripening, smaller particles dissolve and supply material to larger particles.
Heating produces rapid phase separation into core-shell or otherwise compositionally segregated structures.
Heating causes a significant reduction in the number density of particles smaller than 5 nm.
Heating changes the particles from spherical shapes to faceted polyhedra.
Particles larger than 20 nm or held below 400 K should remain single phase because bulk sluggish diffusion dominates.
The proposed experiment heats monodisperse sub-5 nm particles from 300 K to 1000 K in vacuum while measuring size, shape, composition, and coarsening kinetics.
Bulk sluggish diffusion should have an activation energy above 2.5 eV, whereas surface diffusion should have an activation energy below 1.5 eV.
Retention of equiatomic single-phase composition and spherical shape up to 1000 K, with no loss of the smallest particles, would falsify the proposed segregation and ripening mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and boundary assign a specific breakdown temperature of approximately 600 K, while the uncertainty field states that the critical temperature for this alloy is unknown.

The hypothesis identifies breakdown specifically below approximately 5 nm, whereas the boundary states that the hypothesis applies to all particles below 10 nm without clearly distinguishing the 5-10 nm regime.
